summary: Immutable Infrastructure product documentation covering Cluster API-based Kubernetes cluster lifecycle management, provider support, installation, upgrades, node operations, machine configuration, and Kubernetes API references.

docs/en/apis/cluster_api/addons/clusterr.description: CRD reference page for `ClusterResourceSet` in the `addons.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1` API group, rendered from the live `clusterresourcesets.addons.cluster.x-k8s.io` CRD schema. ClusterResourceSet selects workload clusters via label selectors and applies a set of ConfigMap/Secret-packaged resources (CNI plugins, storage drivers, other add-ons) to them.

CRD reference page for `ClusterResourceSetBinding` in the `addons.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1` API group, generated from the `clusterresourcesetbindings.addons.cluster.x-k8s.io` CRD. Each binding tracks, per workload cluster, which ClusterResourceSet resources have already been applied and their hashes so add-ons aren't re-applied on every reconciliation.

docs/en/apis/cluster_api/addons/index.md.description: Index for the Cluster API Add-on APIs section, covering the `addons.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1` CRDs (`ClusterResourceSet`, `ClusterResourceSetBinding`) used to distribute Kubernetes add-on manifests to fleets of Cluster API workload clusters.

docs/en/apis/cluster_api/core/cluster.md.description: CRD reference page for the core `Cluster` resource in `cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`, rendered from the `clusters.cluster.x-k8s.io` schema. The Cluster object is the top-level Cluster API resource that ties together an infrastructure provider reference, a control plane reference, networking configuration (pod/service CIDRs, service domain), and topology when using ClusterClass.

docs/en/apis/cluster_api/core/clustercla.description: CRD reference page for `ClusterClass` in `cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`, generated from `clusterclasses.cluster.x-k8s.io`. ClusterClass defines a reusable cluster template with infrastructure/control-plane/worker class references, variables, and JSON-patch-based variants, enabling managed-topology clusters to be instantiated declaratively from a single class.

docs/en/apis/cluster_api/core/index.mdx.description: Index for the Cluster API Core APIs section, listing the `cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1` CRDs: `Cluster`, `ClusterClass`, `Machine`, `MachineSet`, `MachineDeployment`, `MachinePool`, `MachineHealthCheck`, and `MachineDrainRule`.

docs/en/apis/cluster_api/core/machine.md.description: CRD reference page for `Machine` in `cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`, rendered from the `machines.cluster.x-k8s.io` schema. A Machine represents the desired state of one Kubernetes node, pairing an infrastructure-provider machine reference with a bootstrap data source and surfacing provider IDs, node refs, and conditions for that node's lifecycle.

docs/en/apis/cluster_api/core/machinedep.description: CRD reference page for `MachineDeployment` in `cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`, generated from `machinedeployments.cluster.x-k8s.io`. MachineDeployment provides rolling-update and rollback semantics for worker nodes by managing the underlying MachineSets, analogous to how Kubernetes Deployments manage ReplicaSets of Pods.

docs/en/apis/cluster_api/core/machinedra.description: CRD reference page for `MachineDrainRule` in `cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`, rendered from `machinedrainrules.cluster.x-k8s.io`. MachineDrainRule customises how Cluster API drains nodes during deletion or upgrade, letting operators match pods (by namespace/label selectors) and override the default drain behaviour with `Drain`, `Skip`, or `WaitCompleted` semantics.

docs/en/apis/cluster_api/core/machinehea.description: CRD reference page for `MachineHealthCheck` in `cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`, generated from `machinehealthchecks.cluster.x-k8s.io`. MachineHealthCheck watches Machines against unhealthy-condition rules (e.g. `Ready=False` for N minutes) and triggers automatic remediation, deleting unhealthy Machines so the owning MachineSet/MachineDeployment can re-provision replacements.

docs/en/apis/cluster_api/core/machinepoo.description: CRD reference page for `MachinePool` in `cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`, rendered from `machinepools.cluster.x-k8s.io`. MachinePool delegates lifecycle management of a group of worker nodes to the underlying cloud provider's native scaling primitives (e.g. AWS ASGs, Azure VMSS), instead of representing each node as an individual Machine.

docs/en/apis/cluster_api/core/machineset.description: CRD reference page for `MachineSet` in `cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`, generated from `machinesets.cluster.x-k8s.io`. MachineSet ensures a specified number of Machine replicas matching a template are running at any time, providing the lower-level replica-management primitive that MachineDeployment builds on for rolling updates.

docs/en/apis/cluster_api/hosted_control_.description: CRD reference page for `DataStore` in the Kamaji API group `kamaji.clastix.io/v1alpha1`, rendered from `datastores.kamaji.clastix.io`. DataStore declares an external etcd, MySQL, PostgreSQL, or NATS backend that Kamaji uses to persist the Kubernetes state of hosted tenant control planes, with TLS/credentials configured via referenced Secrets.

Index for the Hosted Control Plane APIs section, covering the Kamaji-based (`kamaji.clastix.io`) CRDs such as `DataStore` that back Cluster API hosted-control-plane deployments where tenant Kubernetes control planes run as pods on a management cluster.

CRD reference for `kamajicontrolplanes.controlplane.cluster.x-k8s.io` (`controlplane.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1alpha1`), the Cluster API control-plane provider resource that bridges a CAPI `Cluster` to a Kamaji-hosted Kubernetes control plane. Used to declaratively spin up hosted control planes for tenant clusters without dedicated control-plane nodes; the rendered K8sCrd component lists the full field schema.

CRD reference for `kamajicontrolplanetemplates.controlplane.cluster.x-k8s.io` (`controlplane.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1alpha1`), the template object referenced by `ClusterClass` to generate `KamajiControlPlane` instances when creating clusters via topology/managed-topology workflows. Holds the reusable spec for hosted control planes.

CRD reference for `tenantcontrolplanes.kamaji.clastix.io` (`kamaji.clastix.io/v1alpha1`), the Kamaji-native object that represents the actual hosted Kubernetes control plane (kube-apiserver, controller-manager, scheduler, etcd backend) running as pods on the management cluster. This is the lower-level resource that `KamajiControlPlane` reconciles into.

docs/en/apis/cluster_api/index.mdx.description: Top-level index for the Cluster API reference section, scoping the CRD documentation that follows to the cluster-lifecycle resources Immutable Infrastructure consumes (bootstrap, control-plane, IPAM, runtime extension groups under `*.cluster.x-k8s.io`).

docs/en/apis/cluster_api/ipam/index.mdx.description: Section overview for the Cluster API IPAM CRDs (`ipam.cluster.x-k8s.io`), the provider-agnostic API used to claim and allocate static IP addresses for cluster machines from in-cluster IP pools.

docs/en/apis/cluster_api/ipam/ipaddress..description: CRD reference for `ipaddresses.ipam.cluster.x-k8s.io` (`ipam.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1alpha1`), the resource an IPAM provider writes to bind an allocated IP, gateway, prefix, and DNS settings to a satisfied `IPAddressClaim`. Consumers (typically infra-provider machines) read it to wire static networking.

docs/en/apis/cluster_api/ipam/ipaddressc.description: CRD reference for `ipaddressclaims.ipam.cluster.x-k8s.io` (`ipam.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1alpha1`), the claim object a machine or template creates against a named IP pool; an IPAM provider watches claims and responds by creating a matching `IPAddress`.

docs/en/apis/cluster_api/kubeadm_bootstr.description: Section overview for the Kubeadm bootstrap-provider CRDs (`bootstrap.cluster.x-k8s.io`), which generate the cloud-init/ignition userdata that turns a fresh node into a kubeadm-joined Kubernetes member.

CRD reference for `kubeadmconfigs.bootstrap.cluster.x-k8s.io` (`bootstrap.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`), the per-machine bootstrap config consumed by the Kubeadm bootstrap provider; encapsulates `InitConfiguration`/`JoinConfiguration`, files, preKubeadm/postKubeadm commands, users, NTP, and produces the rendered userdata secret used by the infrastructure machine.

CRD reference for `kubeadmconfigtemplates.bootstrap.cluster.x-k8s.io` (`bootstrap.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`), the template referenced by `MachineDeployment`, `MachinePool`, and `ClusterClass` to stamp out worker `KubeadmConfig` instances with a shared bootstrap recipe.

docs/en/apis/cluster_api/kubeadm_control.description: Section overview for the Kubeadm control-plane provider CRDs (`controlplane.cluster.x-k8s.io`), the stacked-etcd kubeadm-based alternative to hosted control planes used when control-plane nodes run on dedicated machines.

CRD reference for `kubeadmcontrolplanes.controlplane.cluster.x-k8s.io` (`controlplane.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`), the control-plane provider object that owns control-plane `Machine` objects, drives kubeadm init/join, manages rolling updates of the kube-apiserver/etcd, and exposes replica/version fields for upgrades and scaling.

CRD reference for `kubeadmcontrolplanetemplates.controlplane.cluster.x-k8s.io` (`controlplane.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`), the template referenced by `ClusterClass` to instantiate `KubeadmControlPlane` objects for clusters created through the managed-topology flow.

docs/en/apis/cluster_api/runtime/extensi.description: CRD reference for `extensionconfigs.runtime.cluster.x-k8s.io` (`runtime.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1alpha1`), the registration object that wires a Runtime SDK extension server (lifecycle hooks, topology mutation, etc.) into the Cluster API runtime so reconcilers will dispatch hook calls to it.

docs/en/apis/cluster_api/runtime/index.m.description: Section overview for the Cluster API Runtime SDK CRDs (`runtime.cluster.x-k8s.io`), which let operators plug in external webhook-style extensions that intercept cluster lifecycle hooks and topology mutations.

docs/en/apis/index.mdx.description: Top-level landing page for the API Reference section of Alauda Container Platform's Immutable Infrastructure docs, rendering an auto-generated overview of every CRD group documented under apis/ (Cluster API core, addons, IPAM, hosted/kubeadm control plane and bootstrap, runtime, machine configuration, and per-provider resources).

docs/en/apis/intro.mdx.description: Introduction page for the ACP Immutable Infrastructure API surface that injects the shared <AcpApisOverview /> component, summarizing the Kubernetes-native CRDs the product exposes for declarative cluster and node lifecycle management.

docs/en/apis/machine_configuration/index.description: Section landing page for the machineconfiguration.alauda.io API group, framing MachineConfig, MachineConfigPool, and MachineConfiguration as the CRDs that declaratively describe node operating system state (files, units, kernel arguments) for Immutable Infrastructure nodes.

docs/en/apis/machine_configuration/machi.description: Renders the auto-generated CRD reference for `machineconfigs.machineconfiguration.alauda.io/v1alpha1`, the resource that carries individual OS-level configuration fragments (ignition-style files, systemd units, kernel arguments, SSH keys) that the Machine Config Operator merges and applies to nodes selected via MachineConfigPool labels.

CRD reference for `machineconfigpools.machineconfiguration.alauda.io/v1alpha1`, the pool resource that groups nodes by label selector, aggregates matching MachineConfigs into a rendered configuration, and drives rolling, controlled rollouts of OS changes across that node set.

CRD reference for the cluster-singleton `machineconfigurations.machineconfiguration.alauda.io/v1alpha1` resource, which holds top-level operator settings (such as managed component behavior and global rollout policy) for the Machine Config Operator controlling all MachineConfigPools.

docs/en/apis/providers/bare-metal/bareme.description: CRD reference page for `BaremetalCluster` in the `infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1` API group, rendered from the live `baremetalclusters.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io` CRD schema. BaremetalCluster (short name `bmc`) holds the cluster-level infrastructure owned by the bare-metal provider: the CAPI-contract `spec.controlPlaneEndpoint`, a `spec.controlPlaneLoadBalancer` VIP (host, port, `Internal`/`External` type, keepalived `vrid`) that backfills that endpoint, and `spec.networkType` CNI metadata; `status.ready` and `status.conditions` report infra readiness to Cluster API.

CRD reference page for `BaremetalMachine` in the `infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1` API group, rendered from the live `baremetalmachines.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io` CRD schema. BaremetalMachine (short name `bmm`) backs one CAPI `Machine` by allocating a `MachineInventory` from the immutable `spec.machineInventoryPoolRef`, with `spec.providerID` in the form `baremetal:///<inventory-name>`. Status tracks `machineInventoryRef`, `phase`, `planSecretRef`, and bootstrap/plan checksums driving the reprovision pipeline; role and Kubernetes version come from the owning `KubeadmControlPlane` or `MachineDeployment`.

CRD reference page for `BaremetalMachineTemplate` in the `infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1` API group, rendered from the live `baremetalmachinetemplates.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io` CRD schema. BaremetalMachineTemplate (short name `bmmt`) lets a `KubeadmControlPlane` or `MachineDeployment` bind a `MachineInventoryPool`: `spec.template` carries the templated `BaremetalMachine` spec (`machineInventoryPoolRef`, optional `providerID`) together with the CAPI templated `metadata` labels and annotations stamped onto each generated machine.

docs/en/apis/providers/bare-metal/index..description: Index for the Bare Metal Provider APIs section, covering the provider's own `infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1` CRDs (`BaremetalCluster`, `BaremetalMachine`, `BaremetalMachineTemplate`, `MachineInventoryPool`), the `elemental.cattle.io/v1beta1` CRDs it builds on (`MachineRegistration`, `SeedImage`, `MachineInventory`), and the upstream Cluster API resources it composes without schema changes (`Cluster`, `KubeadmControlPlane`, `MachineDeployment`, `KubeadmConfigTemplate`). The provider is layered on `elemental-operator` and Cluster API.

docs/en/apis/providers/bare-metal/machin.description: CRD reference page for `MachineInventory` in the `elemental.cattle.io/v1beta1` API group, rendered from the live `machineinventories.elemental.cattle.io` CRD schema. MachineInventory is a physical host's long-lived identity, created by `elemental-register` and borrowed by one `BaremetalMachine` at a time. Covers the Alauda-fork `spec.observedNetwork` replayed as cloud-init `network-config` v2, `spec.storage` desired state for up to 32 inventory-owned volumes (`Adopt`/`InitializeIfBlank`, XFS/ext4, mount policy, `retryNonce`), `status.observedStorage` from `elemental-storage-observer.service`, provider-owned `status.storage` lifecycle and plan Secret serialization, and the `machineinventories/storageinitialize` approval gate guarding destructive initialization.

CRD reference page for `MachineInventoryPool` in the `infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1` API group, rendered from the live `machineinventorypools.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io` CRD schema. MachineInventoryPool (short name `mip`) enumerates in `spec.machineInventories` the `MachineInventory` names allowed to back `BaremetalMachine`s, each with an optional `hostname` override, and binds them to a single `spec.clusterName`; an inventory must not belong to another active pool. Status aggregates `total`, `available`, `allocated`, `preparing`, `reprovisioning`, and `unavailable` capacity counts.

CRD reference page for `MachineRegistration` in the `elemental.cattle.io/v1beta1` API group, rendered from the live `machineregistrations.elemental.cattle.io` CRD schema. Owned by `elemental-operator` and authored once per workload cluster; the bare-metal provider never mutates it. `spec.config` cloud-config, `spec.machineName`, and `spec.machineInventoryLabels`/`machineInventoryAnnotations` are baked into the registration ISO and replayed by `elemental-register` on first boot to turn a freshly imaged host into a `MachineInventory`; status publishes `registrationURL`, `registrationToken`, and `serviceAccountRef`.

docs/en/apis/providers/bare-metal/seedim.description: CRD reference page for `SeedImage` in the `elemental.cattle.io/v1beta1` API group, rendered from the live `seedimages.elemental.cattle.io` CRD schema. Owned by `elemental-operator`: a SeedImage references a `MachineRegistration` through `spec.registrationRef` and triggers a build of an ISO or raw image (`spec.baseImage`, `type`, `size`, `targetPlatform`, `cloud-config`, `buildContainer`, `cleanupAfterMinutes`, `retriggerBuild`) with the registration URL embedded; status exposes `downloadURL`, `checksumURL`, `downloadToken`, and build `state`. Hosts booted from the image register as `MachineInventory` objects.

docs/en/apis/providers/huawei-cloud-stac.description: CRD reference for `hcsclusters.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`, the Cluster API infrastructure resource representing a Kubernetes cluster's networking and control-plane endpoint on Huawei Cloud Stack (VPC, subnets, security groups, load balancer) and reconciled by the HCS infrastructure provider.

CRD reference for `hcsmachines.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`, the per-instance Cluster API infrastructure resource that maps a Cluster API Machine onto a concrete HCS ECS virtual machine (flavor, image, volumes, network ports) and tracks its provider ID and readiness.

CRD reference for `hcsmachineconfigpools.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`, the HCS pool resource that holds pre-allocated IP addresses, hostnames, and related per-node configuration drawn down when HCSMachineTemplate instantiates new VMs.

CRD reference for `hcsmachinetemplates.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`, the immutable template consumed by Cluster API MachineDeployments and KubeadmControlPlanes to stamp out identically configured HCSMachine VMs (flavor, image, disks, network).

Index page for the Huawei Cloud Stack infrastructure provider, enumerating its four CRDs under the API group `infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1` and linking to each detailed reference: `HCSCluster` (Kubernetes cluster infrastructure on HCS), `HCSMachine` (an HCS virtual machine), `HCSMachineTemplate` (template for creating HCS machines), and `HCSMachineConfigPool` (pool of hostnames, static IP addresses, and persistent disk slots).

docs/en/apis/providers/huawei-dcs/dcsclu.description: CRD reference for `dcsclusters.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`, the Cluster API infrastructure resource representing the cluster-level networking (VPC, subnets, security groups, load balancer endpoint) of a Kubernetes cluster running on the Huawei DCS platform.

docs/en/apis/providers/huawei-dcs/dcsiph.description: CRD reference for `dcsiphostnamepools.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`, the DCS pool resource that pre-allocates static IP addresses and hostnames so that newly created DCSMachine instances receive deterministic network identities at provisioning time.

docs/en/apis/providers/huawei-dcs/dcsmac.description: CRD reference for `dcsmachines.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`, the per-instance Cluster API infrastructure resource that maps a Cluster API Machine onto a concrete DCS virtual machine (image, flavor, volumes, network attachments) and tracks its lifecycle state.

CRD reference for `DCSMachineTemplate` (`dcsmachinetemplates.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`), the template resource consumed by Cluster API to stamp out `DCSMachine` instances when scaling node pools on Huawei DCS infrastructure. Schema is rendered live via the `K8sCrd` component from the cluster.

docs/en/apis/providers/huawei-dcs/index..description: Landing page for the Huawei DCS Infrastructure Provider API group `infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`, indexing the four custom resources it ships: `DCSCluster` (cluster infrastructure), `DCSMachine` (a DCS virtual machine), `DCSMachineTemplate` (machine creation template), and `DCSIpHostnamePool` (pool of IPs and hostnames). Each row links to the per-CRD reference page.

docs/en/apis/providers/index.mdx.description: Top-level entry point for the Provider APIs section of the reference, rendered through the `Overview` component to surface child pages for each Cluster API infrastructure provider (DCS, SSH, user-provisioned, VMware vSphere).

docs/en/apis/providers/ssh/index.mdx.description: Landing page for the SSH Infrastructure Provider API reference, which defines custom resources for installing and operating Kubernetes on pre-provisioned hosts reached over SSH. Aggregates links to the `SSHCluster`, `SSHMachine`, `SSHMachineTemplate`, and `SSHHost` CRD pages.

docs/en/apis/providers/ssh/sshcluster.md.description: CRD reference for `SSHCluster` (`sshclusters.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`), the infrastructure object that backs a Cluster API `Cluster` when the control plane and workers are provisioned on user-managed Linux hosts via SSH. Schema is auto-rendered through the `K8sCrd` component.

docs/en/apis/providers/ssh/sshhost.mdx.description: CRD reference for `SSHHost` (`sshhosts.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`), describing an individual reachable host inventory entry (address, credentials, labels) that the SSH provider can consume when binding an `SSHMachine` to physical or virtual hardware.

docs/en/apis/providers/ssh/sshmachine.md.description: CRD reference for `SSHMachine` (`sshmachines.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`), the per-node infrastructure object the SSH provider reconciles against a target host to bootstrap kubelet and join the cluster. Live schema rendered through `K8sCrd`.

docs/en/apis/providers/ssh/sshmachinetem.description: CRD reference for `SSHMachineTemplate` (`sshmachinetemplates.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`), the template stamped by Cluster API control plane and `MachineDeployment` controllers to produce new `SSHMachine` instances when scaling node pools backed by SSH-reachable hosts.

docs/en/apis/providers/user_provisioned/.description: Landing page for the User-Provisioned Infrastructure Provider API reference, covering the CRDs used to model clusters where the customer brings their own machines and the provider only orchestrates Kubernetes lifecycle on top.

CRD reference for `UserProvisionedCluster` (`userprovisionedclusters.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`), the infrastructure object that fronts a Cluster API `Cluster` when the user supplies their own physical or virtual machines instead of letting a cloud provider create them.

CRD reference for `UserProvisionedMachine` (`userprovisionedmachines.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`), the per-node infrastructure object representing a customer-supplied machine that the user-provisioned provider tracks as a Cluster API `Machine`.

CRD reference for `UserProvisionedMachinePool` (`userprovisionedmachinepools.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`), the pool-based infrastructure object used with Cluster API `MachinePool` to manage a collection of user-supplied nodes as a single scalable unit.

docs/en/apis/providers/vmware-vsphere/in.description: Landing page indexing the VMware vSphere Infrastructure Provider's nine CRDs under `infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`, including `VSphereCluster`, `VSphereClusterIdentity`, `VSphereMachine`, low-level `VSphereVM`, `VSphereMachineTemplate`, `VSphereMachineConfigPool` (pre-defined node slots with static IPs and persistent disks), `VSphereFailureDomain`, `VSphereDeploymentZone`, and `VSphereClusterTemplate` for ClusterClass-driven managed topologies.

docs/en/apis/providers/vmware-vsphere/vs.description: CRD reference for `VSphereCluster` (`vsphereclusters.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`), the infrastructure object that ties a Cluster API `Cluster` to a vCenter server, control-plane endpoint, and `identityRef`-bound vCenter credentials. Schema is rendered live via the `K8sCrd` component.

CRD reference and explanation for `VSphereClusterIdentity` (`vsphereclusteridentities.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`), a cluster-scoped credential that lets multiple `VSphereCluster` objects across namespaces share a single vCenter credential gated by namespace selectors, as an alternative to per-cluster `Secret`-based `identityRef`.

API reference page for the `VSphereClusterTemplate` CRD (`vsphereclustertemplates.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`) used to define reusable VSphereCluster topologies for Cluster API ClusterClass-based provisioning. Renders the live CRD schema via the `<K8sCrd>` component.

API reference page for the `VSphereDeploymentZone` CRD (`vspheredeploymentzones.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`), which pairs a `VSphereFailureDomain` with placement constraints (such as `resourcePool`) to target a specific vCenter deployment target for control plane or worker nodes. Renders the live CRD schema via the `<K8sCrd>` component.

API reference page for the `VSphereFailureDomain` CRD (`vspherefailuredomains.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`), which models a vSphere region/zone topology spanning datacenter, compute cluster, datastore, and networks for failure-domain-aware machine placement. Renders the live CRD schema via the `<K8sCrd>` component.

API reference page for the `VSphereMachine` CRD (`vspheremachines.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`), the per-node CAPV infrastructure resource that links a Cluster API `Machine` to its backing vCenter VM. Renders the live CRD schema via the `<K8sCrd>` component.

API reference page for the `VSphereMachineConfigPool` CRD (`vspheremachineconfigpools.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`), which predefines node slots with hostname, datacenter, static-IP NIC layout (primary plus additional), and `persistentDisks` for CAPV machines. Renders the live CRD schema via the `<K8sCrd>` component.

API reference page for the `VSphereMachineTemplate` CRD (`vspheremachinetemplates.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`), the template referenced by `KubeadmControlPlane` and `MachineDeployment` to clone VMs with fields such as `server`, `template`, `cloneMode`, `diskGiB`, `numCPUs`, and `machineConfigPoolRef`. Renders the live CRD schema via the `<K8sCrd>` component.

API reference page for the `VSphereVM` CRD (`vspherevms.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1`), the low-level controller-managed resource that represents the in-vCenter virtual machine backing a `VSphereMachine`; operators inspect it directly to troubleshoot cloning, IP allocation, and power-state issues. Renders the live CRD schema via the `<K8sCrd>` component.

docs/en/create-cluster/bare-metal.mdx.description: YAML-only workflow (no Fleet Essentials UI) for creating bare-metal workload clusters with the Elemental-based Bare Metal Infrastructure Provider: import the paired `base-image`/`base-image-iso`, confirm `elemental-image-catalog` holds every `Machine.spec.version`, then meet the prerequisites — a stage-by-stage network table (DNS, NTP, registration and plan polling on the platform HTTPS port, registry `11443`, control-plane `6443`, and cluster-internal traffic including the Kube-OVN Geneve tunnel), a first-boot firmware-level clock gate, the install device, residual `COS_*` label cleanup, and the `emulate-tpm` decision. Apply `MachineRegistration` and `SeedImage` — sizing `COS_STATE` above the 8 GiB Elemental default before the first install — so booted hosts register as `MachineInventory`, optionally prepare managed data disks, then apply per-role `MachineInventoryPool`, `BaremetalCluster` (`Internal` Alive VIP with `vrid`, or `External` LoadBalancer), `BaremetalMachineTemplate`, `KubeadmControlPlane`, `Cluster`, and the worker `MachineDeployment` — all in `cpaas-system`. Includes placeholder sourcing, verification commands, and a condition-reason failure-mode table.

docs/en/create-cluster/huawei-cloud-stac.description: Creating Cluster API workload clusters on Huawei Cloud Stack through both a 6-step web UI wizard (Basic Info, Networking, Infrastructure, Control Plane Node Pool, Worker Node Pools, Review — requires Fleet Essentials `1.0.2`+, HCS provider `v1.0.3`+, and a `cpaas.io/os-release` ConfigMap registered per Alauda OS image) and YAML: HCS credential `Secret`, `HCSMachineConfigPool` (hostnames, subnets, static IPs), `HCSMachineTemplate` (`imageName`/`flavorName`/`availabilityZone`, root and data volumes), a hardened `KubeadmControlPlane`, `HCSCluster` (provider-created Hybrid Load Balancing ELB with `vipAddress` plus two-IP L4/L7 virsubnet lists, optional `controlPlaneHA` server-group anti-affinity, VPC, subnet inventory, security group), and the `Cluster` with `cpaas.io/kube-ovn-join-cidr` and `cluster-type: HCS`, ending with kubectl and `ControlPlaneHAReady` verification.

docs/en/create-cluster/huawei-dcs.mdx.description: Creating Kubernetes clusters on Huawei DCS through the web UI and YAML manifests. Covers provider gates, DCS API and file-upload connectivity, external LoadBalancer and DCS Provider v1.0.22+ with ACP v4.4+ Self-built VIP endpoint modes, IPv4 VIP/VRID/interface constraints, bootstrap and alive verification, DRS control-plane HA, persistent disks, magic tokens, component-version sources, single-control-plane behavior, and required Cluster annotations.

docs/en/create-cluster/index.mdx.description: Landing page for the Creating Clusters section. Summarizes common prerequisites—provider infrastructure preparation, the provider/version-specific control-plane endpoint contract, and the x86-64-v2 CPU baseline for ACP-provided Alauda OS images—and links directly to the Huawei DCS, Huawei Cloud Stack, VMware vSphere, and Bare Metal creation guides.

docs/en/create-cluster/vmware-vsphere.md.description: End-to-end guide for creating a VMware vSphere workload cluster by applying Cluster API manifests to the ACP `global` management cluster, validated against VMware vSphere Provider `v1.0.16`. Covers vCenter identity, ordered manifest application, CPI delivery through `ClusterResourceSet`, static node slots and persistent disks in `VSphereMachineConfigPool`, control-plane and worker templates, external LoadBalancer and Registry boundaries, verification, and troubleshooting. Distinguishes Registry-served Kube-OVN, CoreDNS, and vSphere CPI artifacts from the exact etcd, kube-apiserver, and sandbox image references preloaded by the OS template, and links the executable template-validation procedure. Keeps failure-domain objects conditional, separates the Kubernetes 1.35 kubelet variant from the earlier-version baseline, and includes creation-time variants for second NICs, multiple datacenters, and extra or raw disks.

docs/en/global/disaster_recovery.mdx.description: Disaster recovery entry point for a `global` cluster on Immutable Infrastructure. Deploy-time DR configuration belongs to the installation procedure: shared Kubernetes API server encryption provider, etcd `serverCertSANs` covering both control plane VIPs and the Platform Access Address, `DCSCluster`/`BaremetalCluster.spec.encryptionProviderConfigRef` or the `/etc/kubernetes/encryption-provider.conf` entry in `KubeadmControlPlane.spec.kubeadmConfigSpec.files` for vSphere and HCS, the `dcs-import-extra-resources` ConfigMap, and the etcd Synchronizer installed on the standby. Specifies the DNS-based Platform Access Address and bidirectional TCP ports `443`, `80`, `6443`, `11443`, `2379`, then details the Bare Metal DR model: split system-agent identity (`splitAuthEnabled`, `baremetal-global-system-agent` on the local API server for Global hosts and `baremetal-system-agent` on the platform domain for workload hosts), `sharedAuthReadOnly` on the standby, the shared ServiceAccount signing key and issuer/audience, the rule against reusing a bootstrap Global ISO after handoff, synchronizer allow/deny lists, failover sequence, and post-failover acceptance.

docs/en/global/index.mdx.description: Section landing page for the `global` cluster - the platform control plane hosting the registry, base operator, cluster registry, and identity stack, which orchestrates every workload cluster's lifecycle - scoping this subsection to the `global` cluster's own lifecycle on Immutable Infrastructure: bootstrap-host installation and handoff, two-phase upgrade, and primary/standby disaster recovery. Directs traditional-OS `global` clusters to the standard ACP installation path, and lists provider plugin installation, infrastructure resources, and workload cluster creation or upgrade as out of scope.

docs/en/global/install.mdx.description: End-to-end procedure for installing the global cluster through the temporary minialauda bootstrap environment on Huawei DCS, VMware vSphere, Huawei Cloud Stack, or Bare Metal. Covers provider-package delivery, registry formats, DCS external versus v1.0.22+ Self-built VIP endpoint selection, provider-specific Cluster API manifests, installer requests, verification, provider-resource handoff, optional DR inputs, and final decommissioning gates.

docs/en/global/upgrade.mdx.description: Phase 2 (Kubernetes and Alauda OS image) of the two-phase `global` cluster upgrade on Immutable Infrastructure, for Huawei DCS, VMware vSphere, Huawei Cloud Stack, and Bare Metal: upgrade Kube-OVN first, then create new `DCSMachineTemplate`, `VSphereMachineTemplate`, or `HCSMachineTemplate` resources for the target image (Bare Metal resolves it from `Machine.spec.version` through `elemental-image-catalog`), retarget `KubeadmControlPlane.spec.machineTemplate.infrastructureRef` and each `MachineDeployment`, set CoreDNS and etcd tags from the OS Support Matrix row, add the `imagePullCredentialsVerificationPolicy: NeverVerify` kubelet patch when targeting Kubernetes 1.35, and keep `rollingUpdate.maxSurge: 0` so pool-declared persistent disks and fixed identities are reused. Includes stage-based recovery rules and the single-control-plane HCS exclusion.

docs/en/how-to/configure-fixed-install-d.description: Procedure for pinning the Elemental system disk on multi-disk bare-metal hosts that share one `SeedImage` ISO: set `MachineRegistration.spec.config.elemental.install.device` to the intentionally nonexistent path `/dev/elemental-install-target` so `elemental-register-install.service` fails closed, then per host mask that service from the Live ISO, verify Live-root and mount state, configure `nmcli` networking when DHCP is absent, wipe stale `COS_*` labels with `sgdisk`/`wipefs`, and symlink the gate to the chosen `/dev/disk/by-id/wwn-*` whole disk before starting the installer and checking the resulting `MachineInventory`. Explains why `/dev/sdX` and a size-only `device-selector` are unsafe identities and why the ISO must be rebuilt after editing MachineRegistration, and requires the same `COS_STATE` sizing as the create-cluster path.

docs/en/how-to/control-plane-endpoint.md.description: Provider-version-aware contract for planning the Kubernetes API endpoint. Defines the external LoadBalancer listener, backend, health-check, reachability, ownership, DNS, and certificate requirements; gives validation commands and endpoint-change cautions; and documents DCS v1.0.22+ with ACP v4.4+ Self-built VIP, DCS v1.0.21 external-only behavior, vSphere external-only behavior, Bare Metal Internal/External modes, and HCS provider-managed ELB.

docs/en/how-to/dcs_persistent_disk_upgra.description: Migration runbook for moving an existing Huawei DCS cluster from the legacy template-disk layout (data disks declared in `DCSMachineTemplate`) to the pool-managed persistent-disk model in `DCSIpHostnamePool.spec.pool[].persistentDisk`, required on ACP `v4.2.1`+/DCS provider `v1.0.16`+ and YAML-driven because the field is not exposed in the web UI. Walks through recording current `sequenceNum` values, computing `slot = oldSequenceNum - systemDiskCount - newTemplateDataDiskCount - 1` to identify tail-contiguous claimable disks, editing the existing `DCSMachineTemplate` in place to drop preserved disks, declaring them on the IP pool (including the platform-required `/var/cpaas`) subject to a strict claim match on `quantityGB`, datastore, and `pciType`, patching `rolloutAfter` on `KubeadmControlPlane`/`MachineDeployment` with `maxSurge: 0`, and verifying claim/detach/convert/reattach via `status.persistentDiskStatus` phases (`Attached`, `Available`, `Error`).

docs/en/how-to/hcs_persistent_disk_upgra.description: Migration runbook for moving an existing Huawei Cloud Stack cluster from template-owned `HCSMachineTemplate.spec.template.spec.dataVolumes[]` to the pool-managed persistent-disk model in `HCSMachineConfigPool.spec.configs[].persistentDisks[]`, for ACP `v4.3.1`+/HCS provider `v1.0.1`+. Covers recording `mountPath`, `size`, `type`, and `format` of preserved disks (including the platform-required `/var/cpaas`), creating a replacement `HCSMachineTemplate` that no longer declares those paths, enforcing `maxSurge: 0`, declaring contiguous per-hostname `slot` entries, repointing `KubeadmControlPlane`/`MachineDeployment` or setting `rolloutAfter`, and reading `status.persistentDiskStatus` phases (`Creating`, `Available`, `Attaching`, `Attached`, `Detaching`, `Deleting`, `Error`) plus `lastError` causes such as duplicate mount paths, size/type mismatch, and availability-zone conflicts.

docs/en/how-to/index.mdx.description: Section landing page that aggregates the how-to runbooks (machine health checks, node label/annotation/taint propagation, DCS persistent-disk migration, cluster-stuck-in-`Provisioned` troubleshooting) via the `<Overview />` component; no procedural content of its own.

docs/en/how-to/machine-health-check.mdx.description: Walks through creating Cluster API `MachineHealthCheck` resources in the `cpaas-system` namespace of the management cluster, both for `MachineDeployment`-owned workers (using `cluster.x-k8s.io/deployment-name` selectors and `nodeStartupTimeout`) and for control planes (selecting `cluster.x-k8s.io/control-plane: ""` with `maxUnhealthy: 1`). Defines `Ready=Unknown`/`Ready=False` unhealthy conditions with 600s timeouts and calls out the etcd-leader-with-kubelet-down failure mode plus the quorum-loss risk for aggressive control-plane MHC settings; reminds readers that remediation deletes the Machine and any node-local disks attached to it.

docs/en/how-to/manage-bare-metal-storage.description: How to manage data disks already attached to a bare-metal host through `MachineInventory.spec.storage.volumes[]`, so filesystems and data survive `Machine` deletion and later inventory reuse. Covers the Observe/Prepare/Activate/Deactivate/Release lifecycle and `status.storage.phase`, the `Adopt` versus format-capable `InitializeIfBlank` policies, stable device IDs (`wwn:`, `nvme-eui:`, `partuuid:`, multipath `wwid:`), the `storagectl render-patch` approval that binds inventory UID, normalized spec hash, initialization counter, and `resourceVersion`, the `machineinventories/storageinitialize` subresource permission, `retryNonce` retries after a fail-closed operation, and protected system mount paths. Requires an observer-capable base image running `elemental-storage-observer.service`.

docs/en/how-to/migrate-hcs-node-fqdn-hos.description: Rolling-replacement procedure for making existing Huawei Cloud Stack nodes return the short label from `hostname` and the full FQDN from `hostname -f`, needed on clusters created before `cluster-api-provider-hcs` v1.0.1. Cloud-init runs only on first boot and on-node `/etc/hostname` and `/etc/hosts` edits do not persist on the immutable OS, so affected nodes must be replaced: add a spare `(hostname, IP)` surge slot to the control-plane `HCSMachineConfigPool`, clone the `HCSMachineTemplate` under a new `metadata.name` (the rename alone triggers the roll), repoint `KubeadmControlPlane` and each `MachineDeployment`, verify per-node output, and roll back by reverting the template reference. Warns that template `dataVolumes` may be destroyed with the old VM.

docs/en/how-to/node-configuration.mdx.description: Shows how to propagate Cluster API Machine metadata onto Kubernetes Nodes by passing `--additional-sync-machine-labels` and `--additional-sync-machine-annotations` (both regex-capable) to `capi-controller-manager`, then declaring the keys on `MachineDeployment.spec.template.metadata.labels`/`annotations` and `KubeadmControlPlane.spec.machineTemplate.metadata.labels`/`annotations`. Also documents declaring taints on `.spec.template.spec.taints` (workers) or `.spec.machineTemplate.taints` (control plane) so they apply during node registration, with `kubectl get machine/node -o jsonpath` verification commands; requires Alauda Container Platform v4.2.0+.

docs/en/how-to/troubleshoot-cluster-not-.description: Diagnoses a workload cluster that reaches `Cluster.status.phase=Provisioned` and `KubeadmControlPlane.status.ready=true` but whose nodes stay `NotReady` because the CNI `AppRelease` is never applied. Provider-agnostic across every Immutable Infrastructure provider — the reconciler log strings use placeholders for each provider's own object types — with the signature `ServiceAccount "sentry" not found`. Validates the four import invariants on the `global` cluster: `clusters.platform.tkestack.io/<name>` exists, the `capi.cpaas.io/imported` label is present (use `jq`, not jsonpath, since its value is the empty string), exactly one `ClusterCredential` is labelled for the cluster, and the workload-cluster `cpaas-system/sentry` ServiceAccount exists. Notes that restarting `cluster-transformer` does not retry a failed import — recovery requires platform support, orphan-credential cleanup, and recreating the workload cluster.

docs/en/how-to/troubleshoot-cluster-stuc.description: Recovery for an ACP-built workload cluster whose top-level `Cluster` CR stays in `Phase: Deleting` indefinitely after every provider `Machine` CR and IaaS VM is already gone, because the `capi.cpaas.io/imported` finalizer is never released on the `global` cluster. Applies to DCS, HCS, vSphere, bare-metal, and SSH UPI clusters. Explains how to tell an ACP-built cluster (both `spec.infrastructureRef` and `spec.controlPlaneRef` set) from an imported Third-party Cluster, which the workaround must not be used on, and the two zero-remaining-resource checks required before patching `metadata.finalizers` to `null`.

docs/en/how-to/troubleshoot-machine-stuc.description: Diagnoses a `DCSMachine` on Huawei DCS stuck in `Phase: Deleting` past the expected ~60 seconds, blocking scale-down, rolling upgrade, or teardown. Reads the `VMStopPending` condition `Reason` (`WaitingForStop`, `VMMidTransition`) to separate a VM stuck in `stopping` — non-`running` `pvDriverStatus`, a pre-`4.2.1` VM template, or a hung guest — from `migrating`/`starting`/`paused`/`hibernated` states, and covers an absent condition caused by DCS API failures: `errorCode 10100116` account lockout (scale `cluster-api-provider-dcs-manager` to zero for five minutes) and FusionCompute delete-only-when-stopped rejection `errorCode 102212808`. Documents the `cpaas.io/retain-vm` escape hatch and the orphaned VM and `DCSIpHostnamePool` slot it leaves behind.

docs/en/how-to/troubleshoot-workload-clu.description: Huawei Cloud Stack-specific troubleshooting to run after the provider-agnostic import diagnostic. Covers the pattern where `Cluster.status.phase=Provisioned` and `HCSCluster.status.ready=true` but `kubeadm init` never completes: `Machine.status.nodeRef` stays unset, `KubeadmControlPlane.status.initialized` stays empty, and `cluster-api-provider-hcs` logs `connect: connection refused` against the control-plane ELB VIP on port 6443. Root cause is a dotted `HCSMachineConfigPool.spec.configs[].hostname` rendered into cloud-init as the POSIX hostname with `prefer_fqdn_over_hostname: true` by provider releases earlier than v1.0.1. Mitigation is upgrading to v1.0.1+ and rolling replacement, not on-node `/etc/hostname` or `/etc/hosts` edits.

docs/en/index.mdx.description: Top-level English documentation landing page for the Immutable Infrastructure platform, rendering a navigation overview component that links to the major sections (overview, install, create-cluster, manage-nodes, upgrade-cluster, machine-configuration, infrastructure, how-to, global, and the Cluster API reference).

docs/en/infrastructure/huawei-cloud-stac.description: Pre-YAML preparation checklist for Huawei Cloud Stack clusters covering every input consumed by the `Secret`, `HCSMachineConfigPool`, `HCSMachineTemplate`, `KubeadmControlPlane`, and `HCSCluster` manifests in `cpaas-system`: credential keys `accessKey`, `secretKey`, `projectID`, `externalGlobalDomain`, `region`, and optional `schema`; API-recognized `imageName`/`flavorName`/`availabilityZone` with per-template availability-zone placement rules and their persistent-disk and control-plane-HA constraints; temporary `dataVolumes[]` versus pool-managed `persistentDisks[]` (`slot`, `size`, `type`, `mountPath`, `format`, `mountOptions`) for `/var/cpaas`; the version and component baseline; VPC, security group, and full subnet inventory (`name`, `id`, `neutronSubnetId`, `cidr`, `gatewayIp`, DNS); the fixed-address control plane ELB plan (`vipAddress`, `vipSubnetName`, two-entry `elbVirsubnetL4Ips`/`L7Ips`, optional `vipDomainName`); `controlPlaneHA` `anti-affinity` versus `soft-anti-affinity` server-group planning; and static IP pool planning with `maxSurge: 0`. Also documents multi-NIC limitations and controller-filled `spec.controlPlaneEndpoint`.

docs/en/infrastructure/huawei-dcs.mdx.description: Reference for the three Huawei DCS infrastructure resources in `cpaas-system`: the credential `Secret` (`authUser`/`authKey`/`endpoint` plus optional `userType: interconnect`|`domain`), authored through the web UI or YAML `data`/`stringData`; `DCSIpHostnamePool` for per-node IP/mask/gateway/DNS/hostname/`machineName`, `additionNic[]` entries (DVS and Port Group, applied only when a new VM is cloned), and YAML-only `persistentDisk` entries (`slot`, `quantityGB`, `datastoreName`/`datastoreClusterName`, `isThin`, `path`, `format`, `mountOptions`) that bind disks such as `/var/cpaas` to an `(ip, slot)` identity so they survive VM replacement; and `DCSMachineTemplate` for `vmTemplateName`, VM-folder `location`, CPU/memory, and the `dcsMachineDiskSpec` system, `/var/lib/kubelet`, `/var/lib/containerd`, and `/var/lib/etcd` disks. Adds DCS-side capacity and placement preflight (`datastoreClusterName` versus `datastoreName`, host `cpuMuxRatio` checks, provider-managed DRS mutual exclusion via `DCSCluster.spec.controlPlaneHA`, diagnosing VMs stuck in `creating`) and cross-cluster shared-storage `location.type: cluster` deployments.

docs/en/infrastructure/index.mdx.description: Index page for the Infrastructure Resources section that enumerates the per-provider preparation pages for Huawei DCS, Huawei Cloud Stack, and VMware vSphere, and the four resource categories — cloud credentials, IP pools, machine templates, and network/load-balancer plans — that must be configured before creating clusters. Links downstream to cluster creation, node management, and upgrade sections.

docs/en/infrastructure/vmware-vsphere.md.description: Preparation and parameter checklist for VMware vSphere workload clusters, validated against VMware vSphere Provider `v1.0.16`. Separates vCenter-discoverable inventory, product-derived version values, and operator decisions; covers credentials and thumbprint collection, VM template requirements including `<clone_mode>` (`linkedClone`/`fullClone`) and `<power_off_mode>` (`hard`/`soft`/`trySoft`), an executable disposable-VM check for locally preloaded kubeadm and containerd sandbox image references, external control-plane LoadBalancer and permanent Registry readiness for Kube-OVN, CoreDNS, and vSphere CPI, CIDRs, VM folder and node-slot layout, machine sizing, CPI inputs, and persistent disks (`sizeGiB`, `mountPath`, `fsFormat`, `wipeFilesystem`, `datastore`). Links optional parameters to the canonical creation-time topology variants, records the Kubernetes 1.35 kubelet-patch rule, and explains same-pool disk reuse, `releaseDelayHours`, provider-managed reclaim, and datastore-capacity checks.

docs/en/install/bare-metal.mdx.description: Installing the Bare Metal Infrastructure Provider as a cluster plugin on the `global` cluster: download the **Alauda Container Platform Kubeadm Provider** and the **Bare Metal Infrastructure Provider** umbrella chart (which ships the `cluster-api-provider-baremetal-manager` and `elemental-operator` subcharts plus the `elemental-image-catalog` ConfigMap), run the shared ACP `upload_package` and `cluster_plugin` flows, then verify both controllers are Running, that the `baremetalclusters`/`baremetalmachines`/`baremetalmachinetemplates`/`machineinventorypools.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io` and `machineinventories`/`machineregistrations`/`seedimages.elemental.cattle.io` CRDs are registered, and that the image catalog contains every `Machine.spec.version` you intend to deploy.

docs/en/install/huawei-cloud-stack.mdx.description: Installation procedure for the Huawei Cloud Stack Infrastructure Provider as a cluster plugin on the `global` cluster: download the **Alauda Container Platform Kubeadm Provider** and **Alauda Container Platform HCS Infrastructure Provider** from Customer Portal, follow the shared ACP `upload_package` and `cluster_plugin` flows, then verify by checking `kubectl get pods -n cpaas-system | grep hcs` and confirming the `hcsclusters`/`hcsmachines`/`hcsmachinetemplates`/`hcsmachineconfigpools.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io` CRDs are registered.

docs/en/install/huawei-dcs.mdx.description: Installing the Huawei DCS Infrastructure Provider as a cluster plugin on the `global` cluster: review Alauda OS and provider compatibility before selecting the provider package and OS image, download the **Alauda Container Platform Kubeadm Provider** and **Alauda Container Platform DCS Infrastructure Provider** from Customer Portal, follow the shared ACP `upload_package` and `cluster_plugin` flows, then verify with `kubectl get pods -n cpaas-system | grep dcs` and confirm the `dcsclusters`/`dcsmachines`/`dcsmachinetemplates`/`dcsiphostnamepools.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io` CRDs are registered.

docs/en/install/index.mdx.description: Landing page for installing infrastructure provider plugins on the `global` cluster: each provider is an independent component with its own lifecycle and version, the Alauda Container Platform Kubeadm Provider is required in addition to the provider on every platform, and the workflow is download from Customer Portal, upload to the platform, then install on `global`. Links to the platform-specific guides for Huawei DCS, Huawei Cloud Stack, VMware vSphere, and Bare Metal.

docs/en/install/vmware-vsphere.mdx.description: How-to for installing the Alauda Container Platform VMware vSphere Infrastructure Provider (CAPV) alongside the Kubeadm Provider on the `global` cluster. Covers downloading both plugin packages from Customer Portal, uploading them, installing them as cluster plugins, and verifying with `kubectl get minfo -l cpaas.io/module-name=cluster-api-provider-vsphere`, the matching kubeadm-provider module, and the presence of `vsphere*.infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io` CRDs. Hands off first to the vSphere infrastructure-preparation checklist and then to cluster creation.

docs/en/machine-configuration/firewall.m.description: How to open additional host firewall ports on nodes with a `MachineConfig` that installs a oneshot systemd unit calling `firewall-cmd --add-port`, ordered `After=firewalld.service` and declared `PartOf=firewalld.service` so it re-runs whenever firewalld restarts. Explains why `firewall-cmd --reload` and restarting firewalld are avoided (rebuilding the firewall drops rules programmed by Istio, `kube-proxy`, and the CNI), how to pair the unit with a `nodeDisruptionPolicy.units` entry on the singleton `cluster` `MachineConfiguration` so changes trigger `DaemonReload` plus `Restart` rather than a node reboot, and why removing a port needs a firewalld restart because runtime `--add-port` is additive and non-permanent.

docs/en/machine-configuration/index.mdx.description: Top-level index page for the Machine Configuration section, rendering the auto-generated overview of child pages (overview, managing node configuration, node disruption policies).

docs/en/machine-configuration/managing.m.description: Task-oriented recipes for authoring `MachineConfig` objects (apiVersion `machineconfiguration.alauda.io/v1alpha1`, Ignition 3.4.0) targeted at machine-config pools via the `machineconfiguration.alauda.io/role` label. Shows three examples: deploying a custom `/etc/chrony.conf` from a base64-encoded Ignition file source, paired with a `nodeDisruptionPolicy` on that path running `DaemonReload` plus `Restart` of `chronyd.service` (which has no reload action) once it appears in `status.nodeDisruptionPolicyStatus`; disabling `chronyd.service` through a systemd unit override; and installing an SSH authorized key for the `boot` user, the only supported account. Also explains recovering a `Degraded` node from configuration drift either by hand-reverting files or by creating `/run/machine-config-daemon-force` to force the daemon to re-apply and reboot.

docs/en/machine-configuration/node_disru.description: Explains how to author `nodeDisruptionPolicy` and `defaultNodeDisruptionPolicySpecAction` fields on the singleton cluster-wide `MachineConfiguration` CR (kind `MachineConfiguration`, name `cluster`, in `cpaas-system`) to control what happens when files, systemd units, or SSH keys change, and how the validated policy is echoed into `status.nodeDisruptionPolicyStatus`. Enumerates the available actions (`Reboot`, `None`, `Drain`, `Restart`, `DaemonReload`), shows the installed defaults (no action for files, drain+reboot for units, no action for sshkey) and warns that a file-only `MachineConfig` therefore lands on disk without restarting the affected service, and gives examples for switching all file changes to `Reboot` or routing a specific path such as `/usr/local/bin/myapp.sh` to `DaemonReload` plus a targeted `Restart` of `myapp.service` without rebooting.

docs/en/machine-configuration/overview.m.description: Conceptual reference for Machine Configuration, defining the `MachineConfig` and `MachineConfigPool` CRDs, the auto-created `master`/`worker` pools and `00-master`/`00-worker` configs, custom worker pool inheritance, the rendered `render-<pool>-<hash>` config flow, the cordon/drain/apply/reboot/uncordon update sequence executed by `machine-config-daemon`, drift detection that marks nodes `Degraded`, the status inspection queries, and a link to the release notes.

docs/en/machine-configuration/sysctl.mdx.description: How to set node-level kernel parameters that cannot come from a Pod's `securityContext.sysctls`, by writing a base64-encoded Ignition drop-in under `/etc/sysctl.d/` with a `MachineConfig` targeted by the `machineconfiguration.alauda.io/role` label. The worked example raises `net.ipv4.neigh.default.gc_thresh1`/`gc_thresh2`/`gc_thresh3` to resolve `neighbour table overflow` on large clusters. Because the default disruption action for file changes is `None`, it pairs the file with a `nodeDisruptionPolicy.files` entry that restarts `systemd-sysctl.service` so the value applies without a reboot, and insists the policy appear in `status.nodeDisruptionPolicyStatus` before the `MachineConfig` is applied.

docs/en/manage-nodes/bare-metal.mdx.description: Worker node operations on the bare-metal provider: deploy, scale, replace failed hosts, and swap templates through Cluster API `Machine` objects, where the provider binds each `Machine` to one `MachineInventory` and drives the host with `clean` and `reprovision` plans. Covers the four-resource model (`MachineInventoryPool`, pool-only `BaremetalMachineTemplate`, a `KubeadmConfigTemplate` whose hostname, `provider-id`, and `criSocket` the provider normalizes, and a `MachineDeployment` requiring `maxSurge: 0` with `maxUnavailable` greater than zero), `elemental-image-catalog` version keys, `StoragePrepared`/`StorageActive` gating of allocation, targeted removal via the `cluster.x-k8s.io/delete-machine` annotation, the `baremetal.alauda.io/*` inventory annotations, and a condition-based failure-mode table. Points hosts added after delivery at the same first-boot network and clock prerequisites as the original nodes.

docs/en/manage-nodes/huawei-cloud-stack..description: Two paths for managing HCS worker nodes. The web UI Node Pools tab (Fleet Essentials `1.0.2`+ and HCS provider `v1.0.3`+) views control plane and worker pools, adds or deletes worker pools with a per-pool Availability Zone, and edits reserved static IPs through the Update Config Pool / Manage IPs dialog. The YAML path builds an `HCSMachineConfigPool` (hostname, `subnetName`/`subnetId` selector, static `ipAddress`, `persistentDisks[]` keyed by `(hostname, slot)` for `/var/cpaas`), an `HCSMachineTemplate` (provider-recognized `flavorName`/`availabilityZone`, `rootVolume`, ephemeral `dataVolumes[]` for `/var/lib/kubelet` and `/var/lib/containerd`), a `KubeadmConfigTemplate` wiring the controller-injected `kubelet.crt`/`kubelet.key`, and a `MachineDeployment` for scaling, template swaps, and Kubernetes version upgrades; troubleshooting uses `deployment/hcs-controller-manager` logs.

docs/en/manage-nodes/huawei-dcs.mdx.description: Operations guide for DCS worker nodes via Cluster API. Defines IP pools, additional NICs, pool-managed persistent disks, immutable machine templates, bootstrap tokens, MachineDeployments and maxSurge: 0; documents the web UI and scaling workflows, and explains that a dedicated /var/lib/containerd disk stores pod logs under /var/lib/containerd/pods through the /var/log/pods link.

docs/en/manage-nodes/index.mdx.description: Section index for managing worker nodes in Immutable Infrastructure clusters, linking to the platform-specific guides for Huawei DCS, Huawei Cloud Stack, VMware vSphere, and Bare Metal - each covering worker node deployment, scaling, template swaps, and node replacement - and cross-referencing the upgrade-cluster and machine-configuration sections.

docs/en/manage-nodes/vmware-vsphere.mdx.description: Day-2 guide for VMware vSphere worker nodes managed through `VSphereMachineConfigPool`, `VSphereMachineTemplate`, `KubeadmConfigTemplate`, and `MachineDeployment`. Covers scale-out by adding slots before replicas, immutable infrastructure-template and bootstrap-template replacement, rollout monitoring and rollback, and runtime topology changes for NICs, failure domains, and persistent disks. Preserves the existing pool identity when slots or VMDKs must be reused, explains that differently named pools do not share disks and that `releaseDelayHours` is an unused-slot reclaim grace period rather than a replacement wait, and provides checks for pool readiness, Machines, `VSphereMachine`, `VSphereVM`, and Nodes.

docs/en/overview/architecture.mdx.description: Describes the three-provider Cluster API (CAPI) architecture used by the platform: the Kubeadm Bootstrap Provider handles node initialization/kubelet config/join tokens/certificate rotation, the Kubeadm Control Plane Provider deploys and rolls upgrades for the API server and etcd with HA load balancing and health monitoring, and a pluggable Infrastructure Provider (such as DCS) handles VM provisioning, networking, and resource management on the target IaaS. Includes the CAPI architecture diagram.

docs/en/overview/index.mdx.description: Top-level overview landing page that renders the auto-generated `<Overview />` for the introduction, architecture, feature, and providers child pages.

docs/en/overview/intro.mdx.description: Brief introduction to Immutable Infrastructure on the Alauda Container Platform, naming Cluster API as the underlying mechanism and listing the four guiding principles: declarative configuration, version control, reproducible deployments, and stage-aware recovery - reproducible machine replacement for safe template recovery, falling back to backup-based recovery once a Kubernetes minor upgrade has changed control-plane state.

docs/en/overview/os-support-matrix.mdx.description: Maps ACP releases to the Kubernetes, containerd, CoreDNS, etcd, pause, and Kube-OVN chart versions carried by each Alauda OS image. Also documents CPU and image-format requirements, DCS Provider v1.0.21+ pairing for ACP v4.3.2+, and the additional DCS Self-built VIP requirement of provider v1.0.22+ with ACP v4.4+.

docs/en/overview/providers/bare-metal.md.description: Overview of the Bare Metal Infrastructure Provider, which composes `elemental-operator` (host registration, `SeedImage` ISO build, long-lived `MachineInventory`) with `cluster-api-provider-baremetal` (`BaremetalCluster`, `BaremetalMachine`, `BaremetalMachineTemplate`, `MachineInventoryPool`). Hosts are installed once and are never created or deleted by the provider; node attach and detach run `reprovision` and `clean` plans through the inventory's single plan secret. Documents the `elemental-image-catalog` version-to-upgrade-image mapping, `Internal` (`alive` VIP) versus `External` control-plane LB modes, `observedNetwork` address preservation, inventory-owned managed data disks with `storage-prepare`/`storage-release` plans, and the YAML-only workflow with no Fleet Essentials UI.

docs/en/overview/providers/huawei-cloud-.description: Overview of the Huawei Cloud Stack (HCS) Infrastructure Provider: Kube-OVN integration, provider-created ELB for control plane HA, static IP allocation, per-node-pool availability-zone selection, kubeadm-based control-plane security bootstrap (audit, admission, encryption provider, kubelet certificates), and pool-managed persistent disks declared in `HCSMachineConfigPool.spec.configs[].persistentDisks[]` from `v1.0.1` rather than in `HCSMachineTemplate` data volumes. Distinguishes the always-available YAML workflow from the web UI workflow, which requires Fleet Essentials `1.0.2` or later plus HCS Provider `v1.0.3` or later. CRDs: `HCSCluster`, `HCSMachine`, `HCSMachineTemplate`, `HCSMachineConfigPool`.

docs/en/overview/providers/huawei-dcs.md.description: Overview and concept reference for Huawei DCS, mapping platform objects to Cluster API resources and documenting commonly used DCS fields. Covers Alauda OS pairing, DCS Provider v1.0.22+ with ACP v4.4+ Self-built VIP versus external endpoints, YAML and Fleet Essentials management, the Fleet Essentials upgrade boundary, and pool-managed persistent disks.

docs/en/overview/providers/index.mdx.description: Lists the pluggable infrastructure providers and compares control-plane endpoint ownership. HCS creates an ELB, DCS supports an operator-provisioned external load balancer or provider-managed type: internal Self-built VIP on v1.0.22+ with ACP v4.4+, vSphere uses an external load balancer, and Bare Metal supports internal or external modes.

docs/en/overview/providers/vmware-vspher.description: Overview of the VMware vSphere Infrastructure Provider built on Cluster API Provider vSphere (CAPV), validated against provider `v1.0.16`: vCenter template cloning and placement, `VSphereMachineConfigPool` node slots with fixed hostnames, static IPs and persistent-disk layouts, multi-NIC support where the primary NIC drives the kubelet `node-ip`, multi-datacenter failure domains via `VSphereFailureDomain`/`VSphereDeploymentZone`, raw-device disks exposed at `/dev/disk/by-capv/<name>`, and the provider-managed `InUse` to `Released` to reuse-or-reclaim disk lifecycle. `v1.0.16` uses an external LoadBalancer for the API endpoint and deploys no Self-built VIP. Lists the primary user-facing CRDs exercised by the documented workflows.

docs/en/overview/release_notes.mdx.description: Routing stub in the Overview section that carries no release content of its own: it states that release notes are maintained per infrastructure provider and links out to the four dedicated pages under `release-notes/` (Huawei Cloud Stack, Huawei DCS, VMware vSphere, Kubeadm), noting that the Bare Metal Provider has no published release notes on this site. The actual per-tag version timelines live on those linked pages, not here.

docs/en/machine-configuration/release-no.description: Version timeline for machine-config versions confirmed in cloud.alauda.io: v4.0.13 (first published version, consolidating source tags through v4.0.13), v4.0.16 (consolidating v4.0.14-v4.0.16), and v4.0.18 (consolidating v4.0.17-v4.0.18).

docs/en/release-notes/huawei_cloud_stack.description: Version timeline for the ACP Huawei Cloud Stack (HCS) Infrastructure Provider, from `v1.0.1` (2026-05-20, the first public release; internal `v1.0.0`/`v1.0` builds are excluded) through `v1.0.3` (2026-06-27), with New Features, Fixed Issues, and Upgrade Notes per tag: cluster lifecycle on HCS with automatic control plane ELB binding, availability-zone placement, `HCSMachineConfigPool` reserved hostname/IP slots, `HCSCluster.spec.controlPlaneHA` server-group anti-affinity, cloud-init-only node bootstrap, rate-limit-aware machine-creation backoff, and the HCS web UI requiring Fleet Essentials `1.0.2` or later.

docs/en/release-notes/huawei_dcs.mdx.description: Version timeline for the ACP Huawei DCS Infrastructure Provider, now including v1.0.22: Self-built VIP, version-aware Kube-OVN/CoreDNS/kube-proxy repositories, upgrade-time component reconciliation, pod-log placement on the containerd data disk, CoreDNS pull-secret reconciliation, and dependency security maintenance, followed by the historical DCS release entries.

docs/en/release-notes/index.mdx.description: Section index for the per-provider Release Notes pages, rendered as an `<Overview />` child listing: Huawei Cloud Stack (`v1.0.1`-`v1.0.3`), Huawei DCS (`v1.0.0`-`v1.0.21`), VMware vSphere (`v1.0.0`-`v1.0.16`), and the platform-wide Kubeadm Provider (`v1.0.0`-`v1.0.12`). Each linked page carries a version timeline with one section per release tag; the Bare Metal Provider has no published release notes on this site.

docs/en/release-notes/kubeadm.mdx.description: Version timeline for the Alauda-packaged Kubeadm Provider - the ACP distribution of the upstream Cluster API kubeadm bootstrap and control plane providers, consumed platform-wide by the HCS, DCS, and vSphere infrastructure providers - from `v1.0.0` (2025-06-18) through `v1.0.12` (2026-07-28), with New Features, Enhancements, Fixed Issues, and Notes per tag: KCP rollout gating and readiness validation, machine taint synchronization to nodes, platform registry refresh after control-plane VM replacement, standby Global Cluster protection, and CVE/toolchain updates.

docs/en/release-notes/vmware_vsphere.mdx.description: Version timeline for the ACP VMware vSphere Infrastructure Provider, whose version denotes the packaging release bundling the upstream CAPV controller image, the vSphere CPI image, and the Helm chart that deploys them, from `v1.0.0` (2026-04-03) through `v1.0.16` (2026-08-05), with New Features, Enhancements, Fixed Issues, Breaking Changes, and Notes per tag: the `VSphereResourcePool` to `VSphereMachineConfigPool` rename in `v1.0.5`, Kube-OVN/CoreDNS/kube-proxy reconciliation ordering during upgrades, ACP 4.4 system component repository selection, and node address/provider-ID resolution for multi-NIC VMs.

docs/en/upgrade-cluster/bare-metal.mdx.description: Phase 2 Kubernetes upgrade for bare-metal clusters, which replaces every node instead of running `kubeadm upgrade`: CAPI deletes a `Machine`, the provider writes a `clean` plan, reallocates an `Available` inventory from the same pool, and writes a `reprovision` plan that runs `elemental upgrade --system <new-image>`, with initramfs clearing `/var/lib/kubelet`, `/var/lib/containerd`, `/var/lib/etcd`, and `/etc/kubernetes` while declared managed volumes are only deactivated. Covers the management-cluster-first sequence, verifying or extending the `elemental-image-catalog` ConfigMap, the shared Kube-OVN step, patching `KubeadmControlPlane.spec.version` with matching `dns` and `etcd.local` image tags (no new `BaremetalMachineTemplate` for a version-only hop), worker `MachineDeployment` rollouts at `maxSurge: 0`, storage compatibility limits on pre-storage hosts, cross-version hops, staged recovery, plan/inventory verification, and the `no space left on device` failure caused by an 8 GiB `COS_STATE`, including partial-snapshot cleanup and the reinstall needed on hosts installed before COS_STATE sizing was applied.

docs/en/upgrade-cluster/huawei-cloud-sta.description: Phase 2 Kubernetes and Alauda OS upgrade for HCS clusters: upgrade the management cluster and Distribution Version first, run the shared Kube-OVN step (HCS provider `v1.0.4`+ is required for chart `v4.4`+), then create a new `HCSMachineTemplate` with the target `imageName` and patch `KubeadmControlPlane.spec.version` together with the `dns.imageTag` and `etcd.local.imageTag` values from the same OS Support Matrix row. Documents the four disk classes - only `HCSMachineConfigPool.spec.configs[].persistentDisks[]` survives replacement, `dataVolumes[]` do not - requires `rollingUpdate.maxSurge: 0` for pool-managed disks, leaves `providerID` and `serverId` unset in new templates, excludes single-control-plane clusters, delegates workers to the manage-nodes guide, and gives stage-based recovery rules.

docs/en/upgrade-cluster/huawei-dcs.mdx.description: Phase 2 Kubernetes and Alauda OS upgrade for Huawei DCS clusters. Requires DCS Provider v1.0.22+ before Kube-OVN chart v4.4+, uses provider-managed repository reconciliation instead of manual AppRelease source edits, creates new machine templates for target images, updates Kubernetes/CoreDNS/etcd values from the same OS Support Matrix row, preserves pool-managed disks with maxSurge = 0, and explicitly keeps endpoint mode unchanged during routine upgrades.

docs/en/upgrade-cluster/index.mdx.description: Owner page for the two-phase cluster upgrade model with provider-specific Kube-OVN-first procedures. DCS v1.0.22+ is required for chart v4.4+ full-source reconciliation, and the page also documents the separate DCS Self-built VIP creation boundary, repository selection, AppRelease verification, recovery, Kubernetes 1.35 kubelet patch, and cross-version preparation.

docs/en/upgrade-cluster/vmware-vsphere.m.description: Phase 2 Kubernetes upgrade for VMware vSphere clusters: after the Distribution Version upgrade and the shared Kube-OVN step (vSphere provider `v1.0.16`+ for chart `v4.4`+), export and re-create `VSphereMachineTemplate` resources for control plane and workers - `spec.template.spec` is immutable and the admission webhook rejects in-place edits - pointing `spec.template.spec.template` at the target VM template, then patch `KubeadmControlPlane.spec.version`, `dns.imageTag`, `etcd.local.imageTag`, and `machineTemplate.infrastructureRef.name` in a single edit, followed by the `MachineDeployment` version, infrastructure, and `KubeadmConfigTemplate` references. Covers the disk-preservation model (`VSphereMachineConfigPool.spec.configs[].persistentDisks[]` with `maxSurge: 0`), stage-based recovery, and verifying that the vSphere CPI daemonset stays available.
